The Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) has officially released a recruitment notification inviting applications from meritorious sportspersons to fill 521 vacancies under the Sports Quota for the year 2026. The recruitment drive encompasses 182 Head Constable (GD) and 339 Constable (GD) positions distributed across 22 distinct sports disciplines.

Eligible candidates can submit their applications online through the official recruitment portal. The application window closes on 11 November 2026 at 23:59 hours, with a designated correction window open from 12 to 14 November 2026 for applicants needing to modify submitted details.

Vacancies and Pay Scale

The 521 total posts are split between two primary categories:

  • Head Constable (GD): 182 posts, mapped to Pay Level 4 (Rs. 25,500 – Rs. 81,100).
  • Constable (GD): 339 posts, mapped to Pay Level 3 (Rs. 21,700 – Rs. 69,100).

In addition to the base pay, selected candidates will receive Dearness Allowance, House Rent Allowance (HRA), and other admissible allowances in accordance with Government orders applicable to CRPF personnel. Recruited individuals will be governed under the New Defined Contributory Pension Scheme and carry an All India service liability.

Eligibility Criteria and Age Limits

Applicants must meet specific educational, age, and sporting benchmarks to be considered:

  • Age Limit: Candidates must be between 18 and 23 years of age as of 1 August 2026. Upper age relaxations ranging from 5 to 13 years are applicable for meritorious sportspersons, reserved categories, and ex-servicemen.
  • Educational Qualification: Candidates must possess the prescribed educational qualifications as of 11 November 2026. Qualifications and sports certificates must originate from a recognized Central/State Board or be accompanied by a formal Government notification of equivalence for Central Government service.
  • Sports Achievements: Candidates must have represented the country in recognized international competitions, competed at National Games/Championships, achieved podium finishes in Inter-University or Junior/Senior National levels, or participated in recognized platforms such as Khelo India Games and School National Games within the designated eligibility window (30 September 2024 to 30 September 2026).

Selection Procedure

Unlike standard police recruitments, the selection process for this sports quota does not involve a written test or interview. Instead, it follows a structured sequential process:

  1. Identity Check & Documentation: Verification of original documents relating to age, education, sports achievements, domicile, and category.
  2. Physical Standard Test (PST): Measurement of height and chest specifications, with specific relaxations available for candidates belonging to designated categories, hill regions, and specific scheduled tribes.
  3. Sports Trial Test: A purely qualifying (pass/fail) practical trial conducted by a Board of Officers.
  4. Detailed Medical Examination (DME) & Review Medical Examination (RME): Medical assessments adhering to uniform guidelines for CAPFs, verifying visual standards, absence of knock knees, flat feet, and compliance with tattoo regulations.

The final merit list is compiled strictly on the basis of marks awarded for the single highest medal or sports achievement secured during the eligible timeframe.

Application Process and Fees

Interested male candidates belonging to the UR, OBC, and EWS categories are required to pay an application fee of Rs. 100/- directly through the official recruitment website. Female candidates, as well as those belonging to SC, ST, and Ex-Servicemen categories, are exempted from the fee.

Applicants must create a profile on the portal, upload the necessary sports achievement certificate before filling out the form, and complete the submission prior to the 11 November 2026 deadline. Selected candidates will also be required to execute a service bond of Rs. 1,00,000/- committing to serve the Force for a minimum period of three years.

Readers can verify the complete guidelines, check specific category relaxations, and access the application portal directly through the official source: FreeJobAlert CRPF Sports Quota Recruitment 2026.

Practical Implications and Verification Guide

For applicants preparing to apply for the CRPF Sports Quota 2026, careful attention must be paid to documentation and timelines.

  • What is Confirmed: The total number of vacancies (521 posts), pay scales for Head Constable and Constable roles, key dates including the 11 November 2026 application deadline, the fee structure, and the absence of a written test in the selection criteria.
  • What Remains Unknown: Exact dates for the subsequent Physical Standard Tests and Sports Trial tests have not been announced in the initial notification and will be communicated separately by the recruitment board.
  • How to Verify: Candidates should cross-check all annexure formats (such as OBC, SC/ST, and EWS certificates) directly against the requirements listed on the official CRPF recruitment portal at rect.crpf.gov.in before completing their online submissions.
